papers.title_en: Neural-DISCO: Source-Conditioned Counterfactual Editing of Neural Population Activity
papers.authors: Nico Policzer, James Ho, Joseph Soo, Xin Tang
papers.evidence: 神经活动反事实编辑的解缠表示学习
papers.tldr: Neural-DISCO是一种面向神经群体活动的解耦表征学习框架，旨在超越仅预测标签，实现源条件反事实编辑。它将潜在空间划分为各标签特定成分与残差成分，在模拟和真实神经数据上可选择性编辑行为或刺激标签并生成反事实神经响应，同时保留原始活动其余内容。结合特征归因还能识别关键神经元，增强功能细胞角色的恢复，为探究神经编码提供实用接口。
papers.abstract_en: Understanding how neural activity encodes behavioral and sensory variables is a key challenge in systems neuroscience. This requires models that go beyond predicting activity from labels and instead support source-conditioned counterfactual editing: given a recorded source response, we should be able to edit one measured behavioral or stimulus label and predict how neural activity would change while preserving other observed labels and source-specific variability not explained by the labels. Here, we introduce \textbf{Neural-DISCO}, a disentangled representation learning framework for counterfactual modeling of neural activity. Neural-DISCO partitions the latent space into label-specific components, each associated with an observed behavioral or stimulus label, together with a residual latent that captures variability not supplied through observed labels. Across simulated and real neural recording datasets, we show that this structure enables selective editing of measured labels to generate counterfactual neural responses while preserving the remaining content of the original activity. Further, to gain insight into how behavioral and stimulus labels are encoded at single-neuron resolution, we pair this disentangled framework with feature attribution methods that identify which neurons are most important for each label. We find that disentanglement enhances the recovery of known functional cell roles in both synthetic and real data. Together, these results support Neural-DISCO as a framework for counterfactual modeling of neural activity and provide a practical interface for probing how neural populations encode behavior and sensory information. Code is available at https://github.com/TangLab-UBC/Neural-DISCO-neurips.

papers.title_en: A spinal-inspired spiking neural network for continuous finger-joint kinematics estimation from high-density surface EMG
papers.authors: Cristian David Guerrero-Mendez, Leonardo Abdala Elias
papers.evidence: 脉冲神经网络从高密度表面肌电信号解码手指运动学
papers.tldr: 针对高密度表面肌电解码手指运动学可解释性差的问题，本研究提出脊髓启发的脉冲神经网络，结合输入噪声、Henneman大小原则和兴奋/抑制平衡。在23名受试者抓取数据上，该方法在全部六项指标上显著优于六种基线，并揭示了发放率与输入规则性的影响，提供了生理可解释的神经解码新途径。
papers.abstract_en: Decoding simultaneous and proportional finger kinematics from high-density surface electromyography (HD sEMG) remains challenging. Although data-driven methods have shown promising performance for finger movement decoding, their limited physiological interpretability remains a relevant limitation. This study proposes and evaluates a spiking neural network (SNN) that incorporates spinal-inspired structures and mechanisms to predict multi-joint finger kinematics from HD sEMG signals. The spinal-inspired SNN includes a spike-encoding computational model with input-noise variability, a phenomenological representation of Henneman's size principle, and excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance. HD sEMG and kinematic data were collected from 23 healthy participants performing grasping tasks under different elbow and wrist postures. Performance was assessed using six prediction metrics and compared against six baseline machine learning and deep learning methods. The proposed method showed a large and significant ($p<0.05$, rank-biserial correlation $r_{rb}>0.7$) improvement over all baseline methods across all accuracy metrics. Performance improved significantly with increasing spike encoder firing rates up to approximately 128 Hz, and with more regular input spike trains compared with a Poisson-like encoder. In contrast, the E/I balance did not significantly affect the decoding performance of the algorithm. The firing rate and inter-spike interval statistics of the SNN differed significantly across motor tasks. These results demonstrate that incorporating neurophysiological principles into SNNs improves prediction performance while providing additional physiological interpretability for simultaneous and proportional finger-kinematics decoding. This approach represents a promising step toward physiology-informed neural networks, with potential applications in motor rehabilitation.

papers.title_en: New developments in the geometry and topology of 3D head-direction coding
papers.evidence: 用旋转矩阵对3D头朝向编码进行数学建模
papers.tldr: 本文针对三维头方向编码中方位角定义困难及双轴/倾斜方位角规则数学机制不清的问题，提出基于旋转矩阵的新公式和统一框架，揭示倾斜增益的几何来源并刻画其拓扑，将经典HD、重力调谐与DA/TA纳入同一线性代数描述，为三维头方向编码提供了新的数学与拓扑视角。
papers.abstract_en: The head-direction (HD) system is a neuronal compass that represents head orientation in 3D. Its encoding of 3D head orientation can be decomposed into a multiplexed representation of 2D head tilt relative to gravity and 1D head orientation in the horizontal plane (azimuth). Defining azimuth during 3D motion is not trivial, and recent studies have indicated that the HD system implements a so-called dual-axis/tilted-azimuth (DA/TA) rule, a representation that is well supported experimentally but remains mathematically and mechanistically difficult to interpret. Here, I introduce a new formulation of DA/TA based directly on the elements of a rotation matrix describing 3D head orientation. In this formulation, TA is represented by a 2D vector, whose direction encode TA and whose norm depends on tilt, consistent with a tilt-dependent gain of HD tuning reported by experimental studies. I provide a geometrical interpretation of this formulation and use it to characterize the topology of the resulting representation. More generally, I introduce a framework in which head orientation is represented by a rotation matrix and neuronal responses arise from linear combinations of its elements followed by nonlinear transformations. Within this framework, the linear stage specifies which aspects of 3D orientation are encoded, and therefore allow relating neuronal representation to linear algebra concepts. Classical HD tuning, gravity tuning, and DA/TA can all be described within this common framework. Together, these results provide a new mathematical, geometrical, and topological perspective on 3D HD coding.

papers.title_en: Intrinsic Goals for Autonomous Agents: Hierarchical Exploration Captures Future Volitional Action in Drosophila
papers.authors: Declan Kutscher, Reece Keller, Alyn Kirsch, Felix Pei, Aran Nayebi
papers.evidence: 从全脑记录解码未来意志行动
papers.tldr: 针对动物自主性计算机制不明，作者结合果蝇全脑记录与数字孪生，用20种内在动机算法训练层级代理，发现DIAYN在行为与神经前瞻编码上最接近果蝇，能预测未来转向并再现和差规则，表明层级内在动机是逆向工程自主性的有效框架。
papers.abstract_en: Animals have a remarkable capacity for autonomy---driven by intrinsic motivation---without external sensory cues or extrinsic objectives, yet the computational mechanisms behind this ability largely remain a mystery. We combine whole-brain recordings in the fruit fly (Drosophila melanogaster), which reveal neural representations of spontaneous exploratory decisions more than 10 seconds in advance, with a neuromechanical digital twin to test whether optimizing intrinsic goals yields realistically embodied artificial agents that quantitatively match fly behavior and internal representations of future volitional action during exploration. Our hierarchical policy selects from a discrete library of low-level motor primitives, consistent with ethological theories of behavioral syllables. We train agents without external reward using 20 intrinsic motivation algorithms spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency methods. The agents are evaluated in a virtual tethered-ball assay modeled on the fly experiment, comparing spontaneous locomotor statistics and internal representations and decoding future turn direction from kinematics and neural activity on the same timescales observed in flies. DIAYN, a hierarchical competency algorithm learning discrete policies that maximize behavioral entropy and the separability of induced sensory observations, achieves the strongest joint behavioral and neural prospective coding performance relative to flies. Its learned policies closely capture individual variability in fly exploration strategies, suggesting that this diversity serves to maximize state-space coverage at the population level. DIAYN's latent activity also closely captures the sum-difference rule for interhemispheric encoding of kinematics in biological flies. These results establish hierarchical, intrinsically motivated agents as a powerful framework for reverse-engineering animal autonomy.

papers.title_en: EEGBiFormer: Real-Time EEG Attention Classification via Hybrid CNN-Transformer with EEG-Informed Auditory Protocol Validation
papers.evidence: 基于CNN-Transformer的实时EEG注意力分类
papers.tldr: 针对现有听觉注意力支持工具缺乏实时神经依据的问题，本文提出EEGBiFormer混合CNN-Transformer模型，基于自定义16通道EEG采集和频谱/连接性分析实现实时注意力二分类，并利用模型排序听觉刺激生成EEG-informed协议。模型取得91.3%窗口级准确率，系统延迟低于100ms，行为实验证明该协议显著提升注意力20%，展示了从硬件到应用的完整闭环。
papers.abstract_en: Sustained attention is critical for academic performance, yet existing auditory support tools are static and not grounded in real-time neural evidence. This paper presents EEGBiFormer, a hybrid CNN-Transformer model for realtime binary classification of attention states, focus versus nonfocus, from 16-channel EEG signals. A custom analog front-end acquisition board was designed and built to collect a task-based EEG dataset. Before model training, spectral and connectivity analysis, using Power Spectral Density and Phase Locking Value, confirmed distinct neural signatures between attention states, providing physiological grounding for the classification approach. EEGBiFormer achieved 91.3 percent window-level validation accuracy with an F1 score of 94.5 percent, and 88.2 percent recording-level accuracy across 17 independent sessions. End-to-end system latency was measured below 100 ms, supporting real-time responsiveness. The trained model was further used to objectively rank auditory stimuli by focus-state confidence, yielding EEG-informed audio protocols. In a paired within-subject behavioral study with 37 participants, these protocols produced a statistically significant 20 percent improvement in composite attention scores over silent controls, with a medium-to-large effect size. This work demonstrates a complete pipeline from custom EEG hardware through neural signal analysis, deep learning classification, and evidence-based auditory protocol design.

papers.title_en: OneEEG: A Unified Signal-Visual Multimodal Language Model with Task-Aware Mixture of Projectors for Multi-Task EEG Understanding
papers.authors: Jiacheng Zhang, Xueyi Zhang, Xin Lu, Siqi Cai, Haizhou Li
papers.evidence: 统一EEG多模态语言模型用于多任务EEG理解，包括脑机接口任务
papers.tldr: 针对EEG建模碎片化且现有多模态大语言模型理解EEG能力有限的问题，本文提出统一框架OneEEG。通过构建多任务指令微调数据集OneEEG-Instruct，联合建模数值与视觉EEG表示，并引入任务感知的投影器混合(MoP)将异构特征对齐到LLM空间。同时建立OneEEG-Bench基准，实验表明OneEEG性能显著优于现有MLLMs，并揭示了视觉渲染、MoP设计及特征分散的影响。
papers.abstract_en: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used in clinical assessment, brain-computer interfaces, and cognitive-state analysis, yet EEG modeling remains fragmented across task paradigms. Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) provide a promising interface for flexible multimodal reasoning, but their ability to understand EEG inputs remains limited. In this work, we propose OneEEG, a unified EEG-MLLM framework for multi-task EEG understanding. By training on our curated OneEEG-Instruct, a multi-task EEG instruction-tuning dataset, OneEEG jointly models numerical EEG representations and visual EEG representations, and introduces a task-aware Mixture of Projectors (MoP) to align heterogeneous EEG features across different task families with the LLM embedding space. We further establish OneEEG-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating current MLLMs and our method on multi-task EEG understanding. Experiments show that existing MLLMs have limited ability to interpret EEG inputs, while OneEEG achieves stronger performance by integrating numerical and visual EEG representations with task-aware EEG-to-LLM projection. Extensive ablations and analyses further reveal the effects of visual EEG renderings, MoP variants, router behavior, and feature dispersion across EEG tasks.

papers.title_en: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators
papers.authors: Aaditya Prasad, Steven W. Flavell, Brian DePasquale
papers.evidence: 用于神经科学中非线性滤波的神经算子
papers.tldr: 非线性滤波中未归一化分布由 Zakai 方程（SPDE）控制，高维求解困难。本文提出 ZENO，利用物理信息损失优化神经算子近似该分布，并结合 EM 进行参数学习与状态推断。在三个模拟系统上验证准确性，并从线虫全脑数据恢复前后运动极限环，为非线性滤波提供新方法。
papers.abstract_en: State inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters is a core computation for scientific machine learning with varied applications in engineering and neuroscience. The unnormalized filtering distribution is governed by the Zakai equation, a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) that combines the forward Kolmogorov operator (known as the Fokker-Planck equation) with observed likelihood updates. Although solving these high-dimensional SPDEs is often impossible analytically and intractable numerically, advances in operator learning and physics-informed machine learning have made it feasible. Harnessing these advances, we introduce the Zakai Equation Neural Operator (ZENO), a model that optimizes a neural operator against a Zakai Equation based physics-informed loss to approximate the exact unnormalized filtering distribution for latent stochastic dynamical systems. We use this ZENO-inferred posterior distribution in an expectation-maximization (EM) framework to perform parameter learning and state inference. We demonstrate ZENO's ability to accurately infer the posterior distribution and learn its corresponding SDE parameters in three simulated stochastic dynamical systems (Double-Well bistable system, Van Der Pol (VDP) oscillator, and Lorenz system) and compare its performance against established methods for latent SDE inference and learning. We show that ZENO recovers previously observed limit cycles representing forward and backward locomotion from a whole-brain imaging dataset of immobilized \textit{C. elegans} nematodes. ZENO is a novel approach to the problem of nonlinear filtering and dynamical inference through the lens of partial differential equations and operator theory.

papers.title_en: Optimal Connectivity of Random Boolean Networks for Reservoir Computing
papers.authors: Christopher Michael Skeide Vibe, Aliaksandr Hubin, Stefano Nichele
papers.evidence: 储备池计算设计动力学用于时序计算，适用于解码
papers.tldr: 研究随机布尔网络作为储备池计算中的储备池，探讨连接性对计算性能的影响。通过将输入扇出与连接性解耦，系统比较7560种设计在记忆任务上的表现，发现最优连接性随输入扇出增大从2.5降至1.75-2，几乎不依赖任务，但自循环会提高最优值；并提出一个无需训练读出的度量，但不能替代训练。
papers.abstract_en: Reservoir computing shifts the focus from training a system's internal dynamics to designing dynamics that expose useful computational capabilities via linear projection. We study random Boolean networks as reservoirs: cellular automata with random recurrent wiring and a random rule at each node. Their main parameter is the connectivity, the mean number of edges into a node. Without input, these networks pass from ordered to chaotic dynamics at a connectivity of 2, where their dynamics are expected to facilitate computation. How the input is connected is itself a design factor: if the input shares the network's edges, the connectivity sets both the dynamics and how many nodes receive the input, the input fan-out. We set the input fan-out separately and compare 7,560 reservoir designs, all combinations of six design factors, each built as many random reservoirs, on recalling the majority or the parity of a few input bits seen several steps earlier. The optimal connectivity falls from 2.5 to 1.75-2 as more nodes receive the input, but hardly depends on the task or on the other design factors, except self-loops, which connect a node to itself and raise the optimal connectivity. A measure computed from the reservoir states without a trained readout peaks at a connectivity that also falls with the fan-out and rises with self-loops, but does not replace training a readout. Reservoirs of one design vary widely, so a design should be judged by its typical reservoir.

papers.title_en: Open-source Software and Pipelines for Generalizable and Reproducible EEG Analysis: An Overview
papers.evidence: 概述了用于可重复和泛化性研究的开源脑电图分析流程
papers.tldr: 本文针对脑电图（EEG）研究因数据集、预处理和分析工具差异导致的可重复性与可推广性挑战，系统综述了支持透明分析的标准化规范、开源软件与计算流水线。文章介绍了BIDS、HED、FAIR原则及报告指南，梳理了Brainstorm、EEGLAB、FieldTrip、MNE-Python、SPM等主流平台及自动预处理与质量控制管道，并提出标准化数据组织、完整报告参数、代码共享、预注册和跨流水线鲁棒性分析等实践建议，为提升EEG研究透明度、可重复性和跨数据集推广性提供基础。
papers.abstract_en: Reproducibility, replicability, robustness, and generalizability are essential but distinct requirements for reliable electroencephalography (EEG) research. Achieving these goals remains challenging because EEG datasets vary substantially across acquisition systems, file formats, experimental paradigms, participant populations, event annotations, and recording conditions. In addition, differences in preprocessing choices, software implementations, parameter settings, and computational environments can substantially influence analytical results. This overview examines the standards, open-source software, and computational pipelines that support transparent and generalizable EEG analysis. We discuss the role of the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS), Hierarchical Event Descriptors (HED), FAIR data principles, and community reporting guidelines in improving data interoperability and reuse. We review major EEG analysis platforms, including Brainstorm, EEGLAB, FieldTrip, MNE-Python, and SPM, as well as automated preprocessing and quality-control pipelines. We also describe supporting infrastructure for dataset validation, curation, standardized event annotation, and scalable cohort-level analysis. Finally, we provide practical recommendations emphasizing standardized data organization, complete reporting of analysis parameters and software environments, code sharing, preregistration, automated quality control, and robustness analyses across plausible pipelines. Together, these practices provide a foundation for EEG findings that are more transparent, reproducible, and generalizable across datasets, laboratories, and analytical tools.

papers.title_en: Evaluating Bayesian deep learning for robust biomedical time-series classification under distribution shift: A sleep scoring case study
papers.authors: Mads Birch Sørensen, Ulrike Richter, Francois Gastambide, Michael Riis Andersen
papers.evidence: 评估贝叶斯深度学习在分布偏移下对啮齿动物睡眠阶段神经信号分类的鲁棒性。
papers.tldr: 本文以睡眠评分为案例，评估贝叶斯深度学习在分布偏移下对生物医学时间序列分类的鲁棒性。比较9种近似推断方法、两种骨干网络，在分布内和5个分布外数据集上测试。结果多盆地方法最好，贝叶斯模型平均普遍提升分布外准确率与校准，分布内收益适度，并改善选择性预测与分布外/伪影检测，但未改善评分者间不一致检测。
papers.abstract_en: In biomedical time-series classification, machine learning models often suffer from deteriorating accuracy and calibration due to distribution shift. We investigate to what degree Bayesian-inspired deep learning improves robustness through Bayesian model averaging (BMA). Using rodent sleep scoring as a case study, we evaluate BMA under distribution shifts in genotype, laboratory, and species. We systematically compare nine approximate inference methods spanning single- and multi-basin approaches across two neural network backbones on in-distribution (ID) data and five out-of-distribution (OOD) datasets. In our results, multi-basin methods perform best, outperforming baselines and single-basin methods. Compared with point estimates, BMA generally improves OOD accuracy and calibration across both architectures, while yielding only modest ID gains. It also often improves selective prediction and OOD and artifact detection, but, interestingly, not inter-rater disagreement detection.
